function: Learns site-specific analog beam codebooks (phase-shifter beam patterns) for the base station without CSI, using DRL agents trained inside a digital-twin environment (pp. 3-4, 7-8).
system: Downlink mmWave massive MIMO: base station with 32 antennas, one RF chain, 4-bit phase shifters; single-antenna users; 60 and 28 GHz; no RIS (pp. 3-4, 10).
method: Reinforcement learning: SAC, TD3, DDPG agents; digital twin is a fully connected network trained supervised on gain measurements; K-means clustering; online or offline (pp. 4-9).
data_channel: DeepMIMO dataset scenarios O1_60 (outdoor LoS), I2_28B (indoor NLoS), I3_60 (mixed), 5 paths; one codebook learned and evaluated per scenario on its own users (p. 10).
test_conditions: Each scenario (LoS, NLoS, LoS&NLoS) learned and evaluated separately on its own channel set; codebook sizes 4 to 16 beams; no cross-scenario test (pp. 10-13).
baselines: Non-learned: classical 32-beam beamsteering codebook. Learned: traditional DRL (DDPG, TD3, SAC) interacting with the real environment, the approach of [17], [18]; matrix-block twin (pp. 11, 14).
metrics: Normalized average beamforming gain (EGC bound), pilot overhead, FLOPs, model size, latency, and digital-twin MSE loss (pp. 11-14).
complexity: FLOPs 1152NT^2M+64NTM (DRL) vs 1184NT^2M+80NTM (DT-DRL); 4.73M vs 4.86M FLOPs, 18.08 vs 9.56 MB, latency 9.63 ms (p. 13).
openness: none of its own; p. 4 footnote 2 links the Codebook_Learning_RL repository, apparently the code of earlier work [17]; DeepMIMO is public.
q1_support: p. 10: "were simulated based on the DeepMIMO dataset [39]". The three scenarios O1_60, I2_28B and I3_60 of Table I are DeepMIMO scenarios.
q2_support: p. 12: "in the LoS, NLoS, and LoS&NLoS scenarios". Not met: each scenario gets its own site-specific codebook learned from scratch, and no codebook is tested outside its learning scenario; the twin validation split (p. 11) is held-out data of the same set.
q3_support: p. 14: "by codebooks learned through online DT-DRL, traditional DRL methods, and the classical beamsteering codebook (32-beam)". Both comparisons are on the average beamforming gain (Figs. 9 and 10).
q4_support: p. 13: "the online DT-DRL incurs only about 3% increase in FLOPs". Eq. (44) and Table III give FLOPs, model size and latency of the proposed method.
q5_support: p. 10: "were simulated based on the DeepMIMO dataset [39]". Public channel dataset; the paper releases no code or data of its own.
notes: Area 3 (beam codebook design). Reviewer checks. (1) q3 counts traditional DRL (DDPG, TD3, SAC without the digital twin; the approach cited as [17], [18] on p. 2 and the code linked in the p. 4 footnote) as the earlier learned baseline. If the reviewer reads it as an ablation of the twin module, q3 becomes 0. (2) q2 is 0: p. 11 says the generalization capability is validated via multi-scenario simulation experiments, but each scenario is learned separately (site-specific) and no codebook is tested in another scenario. (3) p. 10 says the framework does not directly interface with the datasets; the DRL agent receives beamforming gains computed from the DeepMIMO channels, so q1 and q5 rest on DeepMIMO.
